target_customer: Health and safety and operations teams at port, logistics, warehousing and manufacturing companies
problem: Workplace safety is reactive and relies on manual audits and incident logs. Protex turns existing CCTV into continuous audits of safety rules.
business_model: Enterprise SaaS subscription on top of existing cameras with edge video processing
product_category: Computer vision workplace safety analytics, later site intelligence

founders.name: Dan Hobbs
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no opened source gives background.

founders.name: Ciarán O'Mara
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page and described as CTO in funding coverage. Education and employer details appeared only in search summaries, so they are left empty.

competitors.name: Intenseye
competitors.what: Computer vision workplace health and safety platform using existing cameras
competitors.traction_then: Reported raising 4M in February 2021 and a 25M Series A in September 2021
competitors.funding_then: 4M USD seed (February 2021); 25M Series A followed in September 2021 shortly after the batch

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable real world video detection across varied CCTV sites, privacy preserving processing and translating written safety rules into detections is hard for a team of five.

defensibility.rationale: Accumulated site video models and enterprise integrations help, but several funded competitors sold the same camera based approach.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent absorbing the wedge. Protex raised a Series A in 2022 and a 36M Series B in 2025 and is rated well in a 2026 Verdantix report per its own site.

market_need_then: The YC page cites over 5,000 US workplace deaths in 2019 and about 62B USD annual cost of serious injuries, and Intenseye's 2021 funding signaled investor demand.

branding.domain_note: Uses protex.ai; no purchase history found.

identity.logo: Light blue wordmark, refreshed with a new logo that keeps the same light blue and font (company announcement)
identity.visual_style: A broader brand system covering tone of voice, illustration style and typography was announced with the logo refresh
identity.voice_and_tone: Safety first and mission led, 'protect the industrial workforce' (YC page)

brand_strength.rationale: Strong enterprise credibility signals (named customers, a Verdantix market leader mention, trademark filings in 2025) and a deliberate brand system, but no mascot or consumer virality.

outcome_analysis: Protex went from a five person YC team in Limerick to an 18M round in 2022 and a 36M Series B in 2025 with customers such as large retailers and manufacturers named on its site. It sells to enterprise safety teams with a clear budget and a technology that plugs into existing CCTV, though Intenseye and others compete directly. It is active with offices in Dublin and Boston.
notes: The company's press page says 18M combined seed and Series A while Silicon Republic and others call it a Series A led by Notion Capital; recorded as series_a with this conflict noted. Earlier seed money (Elkstone backed the founders early) is not itemized, hence partial coverage. The Series B appears in the ISHN headline and search summaries; the ISHN page was not opened. Founding year is 2020 on YC and 2021 elsewhere. Founder education and prior employers from search summaries were not opened and are not recorded.
